newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen weak, blue-chips weighed by yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen weak, blue-chips weighed by yen.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to retain a feeble tone on Thursday after Wednesday's sharp fall of more than two percent as the strong yen will weigh on blue-chip issues and participants are waiting for bank earnings on Friday, brokers said.
On Wednesday, the 225-share Nikkei average finished down 490.85 points, or 2.41 percent, at 19,841.98, its lowest close since May 9, when the benchmark ended at 19,802.78.
June Nikkei futures finished at 19,820, down 520 points.
"The weak tone could remain in the market today," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
But brokers also said that any fall in the Nikkei 225 index would be supported by investors' bargain hunting.
"The downside of the Nikkei 225 will likely be limited at around 19,500," Ueki said.
On Thursday, the yen's strength against other major currencies invited heavy profit taking in blue-chip exporters, and brokers expected the trend to continue for a while.

On the other hand, buying of issues driven by domestic demand, which has supported the Nikkei index recently, could lost momentum amid growing concern about the possibility of a rise in interest rates, brokers said.
In other indices, the broader TOPIX index was down 6.69 points or 0.45 percent at 1,469.30 and the Nikkei 300 average was down 1.78 points or 0.62 percent at 283.35.
Brokers said the market was still being weighed down by worries over currencies, even though the dollar had rebounded from a low hit earlier this week.
"Stocks took off on April 10 and reached a high altitude. But before flying on, they got caught in turbulence created by the high yen," Kobayashi said.
Automobiles topped the list of percentage losers on the first section.
Shares were also hurt by a newspaper report that two Japanese car makers would limit their fiscal 1997/98 exports to the United States to previous-year levels.

Toyota Motor Corp shares fell 190 yen to end the morning at 3,290, making the issue the fourth steepest percentage loser on the first section. Its turnover of 3.516 million shares was the sixth heaviest.
Honda Motor Co Ltd lost 180 yen to stand at 3,300, making it the fifth largest percentage loser. Its turnover of 3.867 million shares was the fourth heaviest.

Some other high-technology exporters also suffered profit-taking. Hitachi Ltd was down 40 yen at 1,210, Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd was 60 yen lower at 2,090, and TDK Corp was 90 yen lower at 8,500.

Shares in Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) also fell on news that the leading long-term credit bank's London branch had made a 10 billion yen loss as of April 1 from derivatives trading. IBJ shares were down 20 yen at 1,380.
By sector, other decliners were iron/steel, credit/lease, fisheries and textiles. The major gainers were transport equipment, electric power, gas, shipbuilding, and insurers.
Some issues posted healthy gains on firm earnings reports.

Nissho Iwai Corp, a major trading house, rose eight yen to 488 in buoyant trade, as the firm's bright earnings forecast attracted investors. Turnover was 5.511 million shares, making it the third most actively traded issue.
Taiyo Yuden Co Ltd's shares also rose, cheered by its solid earnings report on Wednesday.
Taiyo Yuden, which makes electrolytic capacitors and ferrites, was 170 yen higher at 1,740 and was the top percentage gainer on the first section.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
